"Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say"
Standfirst: "Unidentified projectile strikes King Khalid airport, killing one and injuring 11, as escalating attacks threaten to draw more countries into Yemen conflict"
Photo credits: Social media/Reuters; AP.

*** RIYADH AIRPORT SEQUENCE - DATED LIST (do not use an ordinal; see note at the bottom) ***
1) THU 8 OCT - King Khalid International, Riyadh. Houthi attack. AT LEAST THREE Saudi citizens killed, including a pilot (GACA, via Al Jazeera). Al Jazeera's travel-advisory piece carries a photo captioned "King Khalid international airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, October 8, 2026". BBC refers to "similar strikes earlier this week".
2) SAT 10 OCT, approx 15:00 local - King Khalid International. Houthi missile. 13 DEAD, 308 INJURED (BBC) / 12 dead and 300+ injured initially, rising to 13 after an Indian national died of his injuries on Sunday (Al Jazeera, Guardian). Deadliest single attack on a Gulf Arab country since the Israel/US-Iran war began. gov.uk FCDO confirms: "a serious incident at King Khalid International Airport on 10 October 2026 at approximately 1500 (local time)".
3) SUN 11 OCT, approx 20:30 local / 17:30 GMT - King Khalid International, TERMINALS 3 AND 4 (domestic flights). UNIDENTIFIED projectile, fire started. ONE DEAD (a Pakistani resident) and 11 INJURED, per GACA. Air defences ALSO intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity. *** NOT CLAIMED by any group at the time of writing *** - Guardian calls it an "unidentified projectile"; Al Jazeera says "The Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes before Sunday's" and "has yet to be claimed by any group". The BBC's wording ("second Houthi strike") attributes it to the Houthis; the Guardian and Al Jazeera do not. SAFEST: attribute the projectile, not the author.
4) SUN 11 OCT evening - KING FAHD INTERNATIONAL, DAMMAM (eastern Saudi Arabia). A DIFFERENT AIRPORT, counted SEPARATELY from the Riyadh strikes. Saudi authorities confirmed it was attacked; GACA on X: "The assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of airport facilities were still under way, in coordination with the relevant authorities." Houthi military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said they had also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport. This is the Dammam attack we carried last night.

CUMULATIVE COUNTS AS THE OUTLETS PUT THEM (they do not agree, so quote rather than compute):
- BBC headline: "second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport IN TWO DAYS" - narrow, correct for Sat+Sun only. NOT a cumulative total.
- Al Jazeera: "The Riyadh airport has been struck FOUR TIMES IN THE PAST FIVE DAYS."
- Al Jazeera (travel piece): "FIVE ATTACKS ON ITS AIRPORTS IN LESS THAN A WEEK" (Riyadh + Dammam combined).
- Guardian: "the latest of SEVERAL ATTACKS on the airport in the past week."
*** RECOMMENDATION: do NOT write "third strike" - no approved outlet supports that ordinal. Use the Guardian's "the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week", or the BBC's "second in two days", or Al Jazeera's "struck four times in five days". The brief's "third" appears to have come from counting Thu/Sat/Sun and misses a fourth Riyadh strike Al Jazeera counts. ***

OTHER DETAIL FROM THIS PIECE:
Saudi authorities extended the closure of the airport and said SCHOOLS WOULD BE MOVED ONLINE UNTIL THURSDAY.
Dead in Saturday's missile strike: four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese.
British embassy in Saudi Arabia, on X: advised against all but essential travel to Jeddah and Dammam and to avoid almost all airports.
Trump on Saturday: weighing whether to join the Saudi campaign in Yemen, telling reporters: "We're going to look into it." Said he would speak to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
Maj Gen TURKI AL-MALIKI, Saudi-led coalition spokesman, Saturday night: the coalition would "respond firmly".
HOUTHI THREAT (on X, Sunday): "We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theatre of operations for our forces." Said "the worst is yet to come" if Saudi military action in Yemen continued.
US POSTURE: about 200 US MILITARY ADVISERS stationed in Saudi Arabia; US already assisting with intelligence cooperation and targeting but has not directly taken part in fighting the Houthis.
KEY FIGURE FOR BRITISH READERS: direct US involvement could lead the Houthis to resume targeting ships in the BAB AL-MANDAB STRAIT, "through which about 10% OF GLOBAL MARITIME GOODS transit."
UNVERIFIED/HOUTHI CLAIM: the Houthis said a Saudi airstrike on Sana'a on Sunday hit a home and killed a child, injuring six others. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed; BBC unable to verify.
NOTE ON WAR START DATE: Guardian says the war with Iran started in MARCH; BBC and Al Jazeera say FEBRUARY ("late February"). Prefer February (two outlets).
